narrative.overview: The incumbent world reads as a well-kept technical readout: cool slate grounds, a single teal accent for settled state, a burnt-orange accent for what is happening right now, and everything else in greys. It behaves like a tidied-up debugger rather than a teaching artifact or an editorial page. Density is moderate-to-high and uniform. Every page is a vertical stack of bordered panels of equal visual weight, repeated so literally across all five steppers that the pages are hard to tell apart at a glance. The type pairing does most of the personality work; the palette carries almost none, and motion is effectively absent.
keyCharacteristics: Cool blue-grey neutrals throughout; no warm tone anywhere
One structural idiom (the bordered panel) reused for every role
Semantic color carries state: teal = resolved, orange = active, blue = origin
Monospace for all data, numbers and code; never for prose
Flat by default, with one shared ambient shadow on containers
Full light/dark parity through a three-block token pattern

rules.name: The Two-Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal and orange are the only accents allowed to carry meaning site-wide. Teal means settled, orange means active. Any further hue must be justified by a third identity on that specific page, and is local to it.

rules.name: The Cool-Only Rule
rules.body: Every neutral is blue-biased. No warm grey, cream or paper tone exists anywhere in the incumbent system.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks something the program actually computed: a value, a line of code, an index, a count. It is never used for prose, and prose is never set in the display face.

rules.name: The Single Headline Rule
rules.body: One display-size element per page, at the top. Everything below it steps down to 22px or smaller.

rules.name: The One-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The system has exactly one shadow token and it never changes on interaction. Hover moves a border color, never elevation.

dos: Do define the complete light palette on bare :root, then redefine only the tokens under @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) guarded by :root:not([data-theme="light"]), and again under :root[data-theme="dark"].
Do give body an explicit token background.
Do put every wide element (code, tree, diagram) in its own overflow-x: auto container.
Do use monospace for every computed value, and tabular numerals wherever digits change in place.
Do express state with both color and a second channel (border weight, dash pattern, position) so it survives color-blindness.
donts: Don't duplicate the token block per page. Six copies already drifted: --down and --blue are the same color under two names.
Don't add a third semantic accent without a page-specific identity to justify it.
Don't convey state by fill color alone.
Don't reach for shadow on hover; the system moves borders instead.
